meta.description: Exceedance tables for Dryspell parametric weather cover, derived from real daily precipitation history.

power.name: NASA POWER (MERRA-2 / GPM IMERG, PRECTOTCORR)
power.licence: Free and open; cite NASA POWER with version and access date

meta.settlement: Each source computes the season statistic independently. Each reading is multiplied by its published calibration factor (calibration_*_ppm / 1e6) and the settlement value is the median (mean of the two) of the calibrated readings.
meta.calibration: Raw ERA5 and NASA POWER rainfall differ structurally (up to 2x in some places). Factors scale each source to the pooled 1991-2025 mean of the two for that location, season and peril, so neither source is favoured. This is a v1 parameter set by the deployer.
meta.offering_rule: A peril is offered only where the two sources' season statistics correlate at or above 0.4; below that the oracle would mostly average noise. Non-offered tables are kept for transparency (offered: false).

perils.drought: Pays when the season rainfall total is at or below the trigger (mm).
perils.flood: Pays when the maximum rolling 3-day rainfall within the season is at or above the trigger (mm).

fields.calibration_era5_ppm: Multiplier (parts per million) applied to the raw ERA5 reading before the median.
fields.calibration_power_ppm: Multiplier (parts per million) applied to the raw NASA POWER reading before the median.
fields.p_ppm: Fitted probability (parts per million) that the settlement value crosses the level in a season. Used for pricing.
fields.p_era5_ppm: Same, fitted to the ERA5 series alone.
fields.p_power_ppm: Same, fitted to the NASA POWER series alone.
fields.p_empirical_ppm: Raw historical frequency of the settlement value crossing the level (no smoothing).
fields.se_ppm: Standard error of p_ppm from 500 bootstrap resamples of the seasons. Used for the risk margin.
fields.source_split_ppm: Share of seasons in which exactly one of the two sources would have triggered (dispute-prone cases).

method.drought: Gamma distribution, maximum-likelihood fit (Thom approximation) on season totals.
method.flood: Gumbel distribution, L-moment fit on seasonal maximum 3-day rainfall.
method.levels: Whole-mm trigger levels placed where the fitted probability equals each grid point.
caveats: About 35 seasons per place: tail probabilities carry real sampling error (see se_ppm).
Stationary climate assumed; no trend or ENSO conditioning.
Reanalysis and satellite-blend grids are tens of kilometres wide; they miss local convective extremes (basis risk).

locations.name: Kano
locations.note: Sahel-edge cereal belt; a single monsoon season decides the harvest.

locations.name: Niamey
locations.note: Rain-fed millet and sorghum; frequent drought years and river floods.

locations.name: Tamale
locations.note: Northern Ghana maize, yam and groundnut farming on one rainy season.

locations.name: Garissa
locations.note: Arid and semi-arid pastoral land; two short rainy seasons, recurrent drought.

locations.name: Dodoma
locations.note: Central Tanzania maize and sunflower; one long season that crosses new year.

locations.name: Gulu
locations.note: Northern Uganda smallholders; two cropping seasons a year.

locations.name: Jodhpur
locations.note: Thar-desert margin; monsoon failure is the central farm risk.

locations.name: Latur
locations.note: Marathwada kharif farming; repeated drought years.

locations.name: Sylhet
locations.note: Among the wettest lowlands on Earth; flash floods wipe out the boro and aman crops.

locations.name: Khon Kaen
locations.note: Isan rain-fed rice and cassava; both dry spells and floods hit yields.

locations.name: Can Tho
locations.note: Mekong Delta rice basket; wet-season storms and flooding.

locations.name: Iloilo
locations.note: Western Visayas rice and sugar; typhoon-season rainfall extremes.
